issues.detail: The Vietnamese adds 'chính' (self/own) to 'trong chính mình Ngài', which is not present in the Greek 'εν εαυτω'. While it clarifies the reflexive nature, it technically adds an emphatic component not in the source.

The Vietnamese 'Ngài sẽ lập tức làm vinh hiển Ngài' (He will immediately glorify Him) fails to specify *who* is doing the glorifying. The Greek 'ευθυς δοξασει αυτον' follows the previous clause where 'ο θεος' (God) is the subject, but the Vietnamese phrasing makes it sound like a general 'He', potentially losing the clear continuity of God as the actor.
